claims.text: The starting nanoparticles are near-equiatomic, compositionally uniform, single-phase multi-element solid solutions.
Rapid post-synthesis cooling kinetically locks in a metastable, homogeneous high-entropy solid solution in multi-element nanoparticles.
Surface passivation helps preserve the homogeneous high-entropy solid solution in the nanoparticles.
The combination of quenching and passivation suppresses high-temperature phase segregation.
The combination of quenching and passivation suppresses high-temperature oxidation.
Temperatures of 773–1173 K represent catalytic service conditions, while 473–1923 K represent thermoelectric service conditions.
Using an inert or reducing atmosphere minimizes extraneous oxidation during high-temperature exposure.
High-entropy alloys can retain a homogeneous random solid-solution structure at operating temperatures.
Rapid quenching limits atomic diffusion and thereby freezes a metastable high-entropy configuration.
A passivation layer reduces surface-energy-driven oxidation during high-temperature exposure.
A passivation layer reduces elemental segregation during high-temperature exposure.
Rapidly quenched and passivated nanoparticles will show less phase segregation than slowly cooled, unpassivated nanoparticles.
Rapidly quenched and passivated nanoparticles will show less surface oxidation than slowly cooled, unpassivated nanoparticles.
Rapidly quenched and passivated nanoparticles will retain a stable single-phase structure better than the baseline.
Better structural and chemical stability will produce superior catalytic or thermoelectric properties.
Slowly cooled, unpassivated nanoparticles are expected to undergo oxidation under high-temperature service conditions.
Slowly cooled, unpassivated nanoparticles are expected to undergo increased phase segregation and performance deterioration.
The stabilization benefit will diminish at temperatures or in compositions where diffusion is too rapid.
Oxidation behavior depends strongly on alloy composition and testing conditions.
